title: Chapter 8: Digital Forensics Fundamentals Quiz
description: Test your knowledge of forensic principles, evidence collection, chain of custody, and artifacts.

questions.question: What is the most fundamental principle of digital forensics?
options: Share findings with all stakeholders immediately.
questions.explanation: Preserving the integrity of the original evidence is paramount for legal admissibility.

questions.question: According to the Order of Volatility, RAM should be collected after the hard drive image.
questions.explanation: False. RAM is highly volatile and should be collected first, before any action that could alter it.

questions.question: Which of the following is stored in RAM and lost upon power-off?
questions.explanation: Active network connections (netstat data) are volatile and only exist in memory while the system runs.

questions.question: A hardware device that prevents a forensic workstation from writing to a suspect hard drive is called a ______.
questions.explanation: Write blockers are mandatory for maintaining forensic integrity during acquisition.

questions.question: Which forensic image format includes embedded hash verification and case metadata?
questions.explanation: E01 is the standard forensic container that embeds hashes and metadata within the file.

questions.question: If a system is actively encrypting files (ransomware), you should always perform a full memory capture before pulling the network cable.
questions.explanation: False. Speed is critical to stop encryption. Network isolation (or power off) takes priority over memory capture in active destructive scenarios.

questions.question: What is the primary legal purpose of a Chain of Custody form?
options: To track the financial cost of the incident.
To prove that evidence has not been tampered with.
To list all files on the hard drive.
questions.explanation: Chain of Custody establishes a verifiable history of evidence handling, ensuring integrity and admissibility.

questions.question: Which Windows Event ID indicates a successful user logon?
questions.explanation: 4624 is successful logon; 4625 is failed logon; 4688 is process creation; 4720 is account creation.

questions.question: Prefetch files (.pf) contain information about how many times an executable has been run.
questions.explanation: True. Prefetch files store run count and last run time, making them valuable for execution evidence.

questions.question: What is a 'Super Timeline' in digital forensics?
options: A timeline that only includes security events.
A chronological combination of artifacts from multiple sources (Event Logs, Prefetch, Registry, $MFT).
A timeline created by a specific vendor tool.
A timeline that covers more than one year.
questions.explanation: A Super Timeline correlates multiple artifact types into a single chronological view to reconstruct events.

questions.question: Fileless malware that runs only in memory leaves no trace on the ______.
questions.explanation: Fileless malware resides in RAM or registry; a disk image alone will miss it.

questions.question: Which registry key contains evidence of USB devices that have been connected to a Windows system?
questions.explanation: USBSTOR stores vendor, product, and serial number of every USB device ever plugged in.

questions.question: It is acceptable to use a software write blocker instead of a hardware write blocker in all forensic cases.
questions.explanation: False. Hardware write blockers are more reliable and are the gold standard for court. Software blockers are acceptable in some IR scenarios but carry more risk.

questions.question: What is the main risk of pulling the power cord on a system encrypted with BitLocker?
options: The hard drive will be physically damaged.
The drive will lock and require a recovery key to access.
questions.explanation: Power loss locks BitLocker-encrypted drives. You must have the recovery key to unlock and image them.

questions.question: Which tool is commonly used to parse Prefetch files and output a CSV report?
questions.explanation: PECmd is the standard tool for parsing Windows Prefetch files.

questions.question: Leaving a seized hard drive in an unlocked desk drawer overnight breaks the chain of custody.
questions.explanation: True. Unsecured storage introduces a gap in the chain where tampering could have occurred.

questions.question: Why is time zone normalization critical when building a forensic timeline?
options: Because different artifacts record time in different formats (UTC vs. Local) and must be aligned.
questions.explanation: Artifacts like $MFT use UTC; Event Logs may use local time. Failing to normalize leads to an inaccurate timeline.

questions.question: The command-line tool commonly used on Linux to create a bit-for-bit forensic image is ______.
questions.explanation: dd is the standard disk duplicator. dcfldd is an enhanced version with hashing.

questions.question: Which Windows Event ID is critical for detecting credential dumping tools like Mimikatz accessing LSASS?
questions.explanation: Event ID 4663 with specific access masks can indicate LSASS memory access, though it requires advanced audit policy configuration.

questions.question: A forensic image (E01) captures only the visible files on the hard drive, not deleted data.
questions.explanation: False. A forensic image captures every sector, including unallocated space where deleted files reside.
